title: Certificates of Deposit: reconciling the Renewal-Date Principal from the certificate's own ledger
content:
## Scope

When a Certificates of Deposit certificate renews, the jumbo test of the new term looks at the certificate's Principal on the renewal date. This rule states how that figure, the Renewal-Date Principal, is reconciled, and for which renewals it is used.

## Rule

1. **Reconciliation.** The Renewal-Date Principal is reconciled from the certificate's own ledger as the sum of every deposit on it, plus every interest credit added to it by compounding, plus every penalty reversal credit, less every withdrawal from it, less every penalty charged on it.
2. **Interest paid out is left out.** An interest payout entry is left out, because interest paid out to another account never joined the certificate's Principal.
3. **Reversals first.** Every penalty reversal owed on the certificate is posted before the renewal is booked, because the jumbo bonus is judged on the Principal on the renewal date.
4. **Every renewal.** This reconciled figure is the Principal on the renewal date for the jumbo test of every renewal, including a renewal into a different tier chosen during grace and a renewal the owner books during grace.

## Condition before the renewal rate is judged

Every penalty reversal owed on the certificate has been posted to its ledger before the renewal rate is judged. Where that condition does not hold, the renewal rate is not judged.

## Ledger worked example (hypothetical entries)

| Ledger entry type | Hypothetical amounts | Effect on the Renewal-Date Principal |
|---|---|---|
| Deposit entries (opening deposit and a grace add-on) | 90000.00 and 3000.00 | Added: 93000.00 |
| Interest compounding credits | 2500.00 in total | Added |
| Penalty reversal credits | 400.00 | Added |
| Withdrawal entries | 1000.00 | Taken off |
| Penalty entries | 400.00 | Taken off |
| Interest payout entries | 600.00 | Ignored |

Reconciled: 93000.00, plus 2500.00, plus 400.00, less 1000.00, less 400.00, gives 94500.00. The 600.00 paid out is not counted.

## Why the reversal must already be in the ledger (same hypothetical ledger)

Had the 400.00 penalty reversal not yet been posted, the reconciliation would give 94100.00 instead of 94500.00. The figure the renewal is priced on would be short by the amount of the reversal owed.

## Points of judgement

**Interest has been paid to the owner's checking account every month. Does it count?**
No. Interest paid out never joined the Principal and is left out.
